pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.

2. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

12. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

2. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

3. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

8. D — Producers

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

10. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

11. B — newton (N)

12. A — 100 °C

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Nutrition in animals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of The Interdependence of Life; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Curved mirrors; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
